title: Training and canopy management — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define canopy-training decisions, sanitation, plant-response monitoring and recovery checks without presenting one pruning/defoliation percentage or schedule as universal.

excludedUntilValidated: fixed topping node count for every genotype
automatic assumption that more training increases yield
copying one lighting/training treatment into every facility

claims.statement: Cannabis plant architecture influences light distribution, microclimate and spatial chemical/yield uniformity, so canopy management should be evaluated against the production objective and measured crop response.
claims.boundary: One plant shape or lighting strategy is not universally optimal across cultivar, density and facility conditions.

claims.statement: Pruning and defoliation responses can depend on cultivar and lighting context, so treatment intensity and timing should be controlled and followed by recovery/performance observation.
claims.boundary: Experimental defoliation treatments do not establish a universal percentage or calendar schedule.

claims.statement: Low-stress and high-stress training should be treated as different disturbance levels with different recovery needs and should not be applied automatically to weak, diseased or otherwise compromised plants.
claims.boundary: The course does not guarantee yield benefit from any one technique.

claims.statement: Canopy work should preserve plant/zone identity, technique, date, operator, removed material and abnormal response so later crop differences can be related to the actual intervention.
claims.boundary: A generic note such as 'defoliated room' is insufficient when intensity or affected plants matter.

claims.statement: Tools contacting multiple plants can become a movement pathway for biological contamination, so canopy work should integrate the facility's approved sanitation and clean-to-dirty workflow.
claims.boundary: Specific sanitizers and contact times remain controlled by the biosecurity SOP and current product instructions.
